problem: Corresponding exterior/interior angles equal, or same-side interior angles summing to two right angles, imply parallel lines.

proof_idea.original: Use vertical-angle equality or the straight-angle sum to obtain equal alternate angles, then I.27.
proof_idea.analytic: Both source conditions yield opposite normalized cosines on the same side. Reverse the first line ray and apply the checked I.27.

# Book I.28, corresponding-angle case: external ray px is opposite to
# transversal ray pq. Equal external/internal corresponding angles yield
# supplementary same-side cosines, hence parallelism through I.27.
thm proposition_28_corresponding:
    ? forall p, q, a, b, x cart(R, R), t R+:
        p != q
        p != a
        q != b
        p != x
        x(1)-p(1) = -t*(q(1)-p(1))
        x(2)-p(2) = -t*(q(2)-p(2))
        geometry::main::det(geometry::main::vec(p, q), geometry::main::vec(p, a))*geometry::main::det(geometry::main::vec(p, q), geometry::main::vec(q, b)) > 0
        $geometry::main::are_angles_congruent(x, p, a, p, q, b)
        =>:
            $are_parallel_lines(p, a, q, b)
    release thm angle_relation_implies_equal_cosine(x, p, a, p, q, b)
    release thm negative_ray_scale_changes_cosine_sign(a, p, q, x, t)
    release thm angle_cosine_arms_symmetric(x, p, a)
    angles::angle_cosine(x, p, a) = angles::angle_cosine(a, p, x) = -angles::angle_cosine(a, p, q)
    angles::angle_cosine(a, p, q) = -(-angles::angle_cosine(a, p, q)) = -angles::angle_cosine(x, p, a) = -angles::angle_cosine(p, q, b)
    release thm same_side_opposite_cosines_make_parallel(p, q, a, b)

        ray_angle(a, p, q)+ray_angle(p, q, b) = pi
